rungs.intro: Maureen has played since the Tower was a bit smaller. She throws underarm for luck.
rungs.beaten: Maureen shakes your hand and tells you your grip is 'brave'.

rungs.intro: Keith measures the oche twice before every throw. He is a tailor.
rungs.beaten: Keith takes it well. He offers to take your inside leg in lieu of a rematch.

rungs.intro: Pauline pulled her first pint at sixteen and her first treble twenty at seventeen.
rungs.beaten: Pauline calls time on the evening, and on your chances of a quiet life.

rungs.intro: The Vicar says darts is a ministry of patience. He has been practising a lot of patience.
rungs.beaten: The Vicar forgives you. You did not ask him to.

rungs.intro: Terry has a nickname, a shirt and a sponsor, who is his brother-in-law's chip shop.
rungs.beaten: Champion of the League. Terry gives you his sash. It says TIDAL WAVE. It is slightly damp.

rungs.intro: Gwyneth ran a school kitchen for thirty years. Nobody has ever argued with her aim.
rungs.beaten: Gwyneth pats your cheek. 'Lovely, cariad. Eat something.'

rungs.intro: Dai has delivered to every house for twenty miles and knows how every dog throws.
rungs.beaten: Dai says you've the arm of a man who sorts letters. High praise, from him.

rungs.intro: Bethan sings alto and throws on the beat. It is deeply unfair.
rungs.beaten: Bethan hums a victory hymn on your behalf, which is kind of her.

rungs.intro: Gareth's hands are the size of shovels and as steady as a chapel.
rungs.beaten: Gareth bows his head. 'Well thrown, boyo.' His pigeons are told at once.

rungs.intro: The Dragon has never lost at the No Sign Bar. He says it is because of the carpet.
rungs.beaten: League champion! Owen concedes with grace and a bag of Welsh cakes.

scotland.name: The Highlands and Islands Darts League

rungs.intro: Morag mends creels and mocks anyone who misses the board.
rungs.beaten: Morag says you'll do. She says it to the dog, not to you.

rungs.intro: Angus checks the ferry times between every dart in case the sea changes its mind.
rungs.beaten: Angus misses his boat but not the point.

rungs.intro: Fiona has stitched half the island and hits what she aims at.
rungs.beaten: Fiona patches your pride with a wee dram and a plaster.

rungs.intro: Hamish spent thirty years with nothing to do but practise.
rungs.beaten: Hamish says the lighthouse never beat him either. He is wrong, but it is kind.

rungs.intro: Isla is the island's best by a good yard, and her boots are full of trophies.
rungs.beaten: League champion! Isla toasts you in something that burns on the way down.

rungs.intro: Siobhán reads the postcards and throws the darts. Both with purpose.
rungs.beaten: Siobhán knows exactly what you scored before you do.

rungs.intro: Paddy Og is steady in a gale, which helps with a heavy pint.
rungs.beaten: Paddy Og nods. 'Fair play, fair play.' He means it twice over.

rungs.intro: Mairéad can sing the whole of a ballad without once glancing at the board.
rungs.beaten: Mairéad hums as you collect, and the whole bar joins in.

rungs.intro: Father Declan says he plays for the soul of the game. The game's soul has a weakness for doubles.
rungs.beaten: Father Declan blesses your elbow. It feels warmer afterwards.

rungs.intro: Cathal has a board in the shed, a board in the kitchen and a third one he won't discuss.
rungs.beaten: League champion! Cathal buys the round and counts it out loud, twice.

rungs.intro: Agnes marks the scores in red pen, and not kindly.
rungs.beaten: Agnes gives you a B+. 'Room for improvement.'

rungs.intro: Stevie ferries people across the lough and sizes up the board the same way.
rungs.beaten: Stevie shrugs. 'The lough was kinder.'

rungs.intro: Bernadette's hands are as steady as a rolling pin.
rungs.beaten: Bernadette slides a soda farl across the bar as a consolation, and you suspect it's a prize.

rungs.intro: Mr Hutchinson treats every dart as a binding contract.
rungs.beaten: Mr Hutchinson concedes under protest and in writing.

rungs.intro: Seamus plays once a week and wins every one of them. Only the lough is deeper.
rungs.beaten: League champion! Seamus lifts the trophy over his head and nearly puts it through the ceiling.
